check_text:
protocol.py: 2 biology problems (2 notes).

1. NOTE CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 95 stocks
   line 45:  p20.aspirate(5, glycerol_plate[name])
   At line 45 the tip went into glycerol_stock (well A2 in slot 2), glycerol_stock (well A3
   in slot 2), glycerol_stock (well A4 in slot 2), glycerol_stock (well A5 in slot 2) and 91
   more while it still carried lb (well A1 in slot 1) from an earlier step (this line did it
   95 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it
   touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from
   them then took the unwanted material along into 2 other wells: wells G12 and H12 in slot
   3.
   Affected: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 87 more in slot 2.
   Also reached 2 other wells: wells G12 and H12 in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 45 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [b5f82510f1cc]

2. NOTE UNMIXED-AT-END: 94 wells never mixed after glycerol_stock went in (1% of the well)
   line 46:  p20.dispense(5, deep_plate[name])
   At line 46 the robot added glycerol_stock to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 86
   more in slot 3, which already held lb (this line did it 94 times). The addition was 1% of
   the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two
   liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at
   the concentration you calculated. If the plate is vortexed and spun down before it is
   used, nothing is wrong; if it goes straight to the instrument, the wells are not what the
   protocol says they are.
   Affected: wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 86 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 86 more in slot 3 after line 46:
   `mix_after=(5, 404)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 404, well)`, with the volume
   about 80% of what the well holds.
   Source: Artel: automated liquid handlers as sources of error
           https://www.bioprocessintl.com/assays/automated-liquid-handlers-as-sources-of-error
   Source: Illumina: normalising library concentrations (pipette up and down 10 times to
   mix)
           https://support.illumina.com/ko-kr/bulletins/2017/03/best-practices-for-manually-normalizing-library-concentrations.html
   Source: Thermo PowerTrack user guide (a reaction plate not mixed well gives variable
   replicates)
           https://documents.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/MAN0018825_PowerTrackSYBRGreenMasterMix_UG.pdf
   Source: Integra: how to perform serial dilutions
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/global/en/applicationguide/master-art-pipetting-and-learn-how-perform-serial-dilutions-our-comprehensive-guide
   [81ddc01b2827]

The Opentrons simulator (8.8.2) passed this protocol with no error: it checks that the robot
can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.

findings.title: A used tip went into a stock: 95 stocks
findings.explanation: At line 45 the tip went into glycerol_stock (well A2 in slot 2), glycerol_stock (well A3 in slot 2), glycerol_stock (well A4 in slot 2), glycerol_stock (well A5 in slot 2) and 91 more while it still carried lb (well A1 in slot 1) from an earlier step (this line did it 95 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the next liquid it touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. Liquid drawn from them then took the unwanted material along into 2 other wells: wells G12 and H12 in slot 3.
findings.fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 45 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids afterwards with a fresh tip each.

findings.title: 94 wells never mixed after glycerol_stock went in (1% of the well)
findings.explanation: At line 46 the robot added glycerol_stock to wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 86 more in slot 3, which already held lb (this line did it 94 times). The addition was 1% of the well, nothing mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with them that way. Two liquids layered in a small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration you calculated. If the plate is vortexed and spun down before it is used, nothing is wrong; if it goes straight to the instrument, the wells are not what the protocol says they are.
findings.fix: Mix wells A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8 and 86 more in slot 3 after line 46: `mix_after=(5, 404)` on the transfer, or `pipette.mix(5, 404, well)`, with the volume about 80% of what the well holds.
